newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish '96 farm trade deficit $1 billion - minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish '96 farm trade deficit $1 billion - minister.

text.p: Poland's deficit in food and agricultural products trade last year reached a record high and preliminary figures put it at about $1 billion, Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski said on Wednesday.

"Preliminary results for the 12 months (of 1996) hover around $1 billion (deficit) in food and agricultural products trade, without taking into account cross-border trade," Jagielinski told a news conference.
Jagielinski said Poland had a farm trade deficit with the European Union, the United States and South America, while enjoying a surplus with countries of the former Soviet Union.
He said one reason for weaker exports had been a strengthening of the zloty currency in 1996.
According to preliminary estimates from the Economy Ministry based on customs figures, Poland's registered trade deficit in 1996 rose to $11 billion from $6.15 billion in 1995.
The same figures suggested unregistered exports last year were about $5 billion, which would reduce the overall deficit to about $6 billion.
